ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gramian volume alignment with a total-correlation bound for six clients
PROPOSAL: Six clients hold different architectures (ResNet-18, DeiT-Tiny, MobileNetV3, ConvNeXt-Nano, EfficientNet-B0, ViT-S) and different tasks (CIFAR-10 classification, Oxford Pets segmentation, NYU depth). Each client sends 256-dimensional embeddings of 20000 unlabeled STL-10 images. The server minimizes a loss built on the volume spanned by the normalized embeddings, and we derive its link to a lower bound on joint mutual information. Clients then add the aligned-space term to local training and we record each client's task metric.
CONTROLS: Local-only training; pairwise InfoNCE over all client pairs; the volume loss without the derived normalization; a centered kernel alignment proximal term; three seeds with paired bootstrap on per-client gains.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: Expect gains of one to three points on the smaller clients, and the volume loss should beat pairwise InfoNCE once clients exceed four. It may fail if STL-10 is too far from the segmentation domain.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Foundation-model clients under a joint contrastive loss with temperature tuning
PROPOSAL: Twelve clients fine-tune complete foundation models (CLIP ViT-B/16, DINOv2-B, ConvNeXt-B, Swin-T, BEiT-B, ResNet-50, and six smaller variants) on CIFAR-100, Oxford Pets, Food-101 and NYU depth, each for 100 communication rounds. The server aligns 512-dimensional embeddings of 100000 unlabeled images from three public sources, using a Gramian-based loss whose temperature is tuned on a grid of twelve values per client group. We compare gains for all clients over five seeds.
CONTROLS: Local fine-tuning; pairwise InfoNCE for all client pairs; a kernel alignment term; frozen encoders with linear heads; five seeds, with Wilcoxon tests on every client and every public source.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: Expect larger gains where a client has under 5000 labels and a flat curve for the strongest backbones. It may fail if temperature tuning dominates the comparison with pairwise alignment.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Embedding-only exchange: bytes per round versus accuracy for heterogeneous clients
PROPOSAL: Eight clients with mixed architectures (ResNet-18, ViT-S, MobileNetV3, DeiT-Tiny) and two tasks, classification and keypoint regression, exchange only 128-dimensional embeddings of a 10000-image public subset of CIFAR-100. The server fits a shared space with a multi-view contrastive loss and returns projected targets. We log uplink bytes and per-client task metrics as the embedding width and public subset size are reduced.
CONTROLS: Full-parameter averaging among identical architectures as an upper bound on bytes; logit distillation among same-task clients; local-only training; five seeds; accuracy-versus-bytes curves with bootstrap bands.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: Expect accuracy within one point of the best baseline at under a tenth of its traffic. It may fail for the regression clients, whose features may need wider embeddings than 128 dimensions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Communication study with compression codecs for client embeddings and gradients
PROPOSAL: Thirty-two clients with mixed architectures (ResNet-18, ResNet-50, ViT-S, DeiT-S, MobileNetV3, Swin-T) and three tasks exchange embeddings of a 50000-image public subset of ImageNet-100 at five bit widths. The server fits a shared space with a multi-view contrastive loss and returns projected targets over 300 rounds. We log uplink bytes, latency traces and per-client task metrics under four sparsity levels and five quantizers.
CONTROLS: Parameter averaging for identical architectures; logit distillation among same-task clients; local-only training; three seeds; per-codec accuracy-versus-bytes curves with bootstrap bands for all thirty-two clients.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: Expect accuracy within one point of the best baseline at under a tenth of its traffic. It may fail for the regression clients, whose features could degrade under the lowest bit widths.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: How alignment quality changes with the number of participating models
PROPOSAL: Train groups of 3, 6, 12 and 24 clients, each client a different architecture drawn from a pool of CNNs and transformers, with a task drawn from classification, regression and retrieval on CIFAR-100, Flowers-102 and DTD. A public set of 30000 images provides positives for all clients. We compare a joint volume-based contrastive loss with pairwise InfoNCE and measure how well alignment recovers the dependencies, using the total correlation estimated on held-out public images.
CONTROLS: Pairwise InfoNCE summed over client pairs; a pairwise loss with a learned weighting; local-only training; a shuffled-positives control for the dependency estimate; three seeds per group size, with confidence intervals on the estimate.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Expect the gap between joint and pairwise losses to widen with group size, because pair sums miss higher-order dependence. It may fail beyond 12 clients if optimization of the joint loss becomes unstable.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Group-size study of joint contrastive alignment on foundation encoders
PROPOSAL: Train five group sizes, from eight up to 128 clients, each initialized from a pre-trained encoder (CLIP ViT-B/16, DINOv2-S, DeiT-B, ConvNeXt-T, Swin-T) and fine-tuned on a task from classification, regression and retrieval on CIFAR-100, Flowers-102, DTD, Food-101 and Pets. A public set of 200000 images supplies positives. We compare a joint volume-based loss with pairwise InfoNCE and report alignment quality per group size and encoder family.
CONTROLS: Pairwise InfoNCE summed over client pairs; a weighted pairwise loss; local-only training; a shuffled-positives control; three seeds per group size, with confidence intervals per encoder family.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Expect the gap to widen with group size, because pair sums miss higher-order dependence. It may fail beyond 64 clients if optimization of the joint loss stalls or encoders collapse.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Three-modality collaboration of image, text and audio clients without shared parameters
PROPOSAL: Nine clients use different models: ViT-S and ResNet-50 for images, DistilBERT and a small LSTM for text, wav2vec2-base and an audio CNN for sound, with tasks including image labeling, sentiment and keyword spotting. Alignment uses a public paired set of 25000 clips built from Flickr30k captions and AudioCaps. A joint contrastive loss over all three modalities is compared with chains of two-modality losses. Each client keeps its parameters private.
CONTROLS: Local-only training; two-modality alignment applied pair by pair; the heuristic regularization used in multimodal federated methods; a control with randomly paired public examples; five seeds with per-task confidence bands.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Expect the joint loss to help the audio clients most, since they have the least labeled data. It may fail if public pairs are too noisy to anchor the audio branch.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Trimodal federation with video, depth, image, text and audio clients
PROPOSAL: Eighteen clients use different models: ViT-B and ResNet-101 for images, VideoMAE-S for clips, DistilBERT, RoBERTa-base and an LSTM for text, wav2vec2-base and an audio CNN for sound, and a depth network. Alignment uses a public paired set of 120000 clips drawn from Flickr30k, AudioCaps and MSR-VTT. A joint contrastive loss is compared with chains of two-modality losses at five embedding widths. Each client keeps its parameters private, and all tasks are evaluated.
CONTROLS: Local-only training; two-modality alignment applied pair by pair; a multimodal federated regularization method; random-pairing control; five seeds with confidence intervals on every task and width.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Expect the joint loss to help the audio clients most, since they have the least labeled data. It may fail if public pairs are too noisy to anchor video and depth.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning of heterogeneous foundation models with private adapters
PROPOSAL: Five clients pick different foundation models (CLIP ViT-B/16, DINOv2-S, ConvNeXt-T, DeiT-S, Swin-T) and fine-tune with low-rank adapters on small private datasets for different tasks: Pets classification, DTD textures, NYU depth, VOC segmentation and COCO captions retrieval. Only embeddings of a 15000-image public set are shared. The server aligns them jointly, and we measure gains over local adapter tuning when 5, 10 or 20 percent of the local labels are used.
CONTROLS: Local adapter tuning; zero-shot features with a linear probe; pairwise InfoNCE alignment; a kernel alignment proximal term; three seeds; per-client paired bootstrap.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Expect the largest gains at 5 percent of labels, shrinking by 20 percent. It may fail for the depth client, whose features may differ most from the captioning client.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Full fine-tuning of heterogeneous foundation models with private weights and long schedules
PROPOSAL: Ten clients pick different foundation models (CLIP ViT-B/32, DINOv2-B, ConvNeXt-B, DeiT-B, Swin-T, BEiT-B, ViT-H, ResNet-152, EVA-02, SigLIP) and fully fine-tune them on private datasets for Pets, DTD, NYU depth, VOC segmentation and COCO retrieval, each for 90 epochs. Embeddings of a 150000-image public set are shared and aligned jointly, and we measure gains over local tuning when five fractions of local labels, from small to complete, are used.
CONTROLS: Local full tuning; zero-shot features with a linear probe; pairwise InfoNCE; a kernel alignment proximal term; five seeds; paired bootstrap per client and each label fraction.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Expect the largest gains at 5 percent of labels, shrinking toward 100 percent. It may fail for the depth client, whose features may differ most from the captioning client.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Membership inference against shared embeddings versus shared parameters
PROPOSAL: We measure the privacy of exchanging embeddings of a public set against exchanging encoder parameters. Four clients (ResNet-18, ViT-S, MobileNetV3, DeiT-Tiny) train on private CIFAR-10 and SVHN subsets of 5000 images. An attacker with 4 shadow models runs loss-threshold and likelihood-ratio membership inference on the shared quantity from each protocol, and we report area under the curve and true-positive rate at low false-positive rate.
CONTROLS: Parameter-sharing federated averaging for a common architecture; logit sharing on the public set; a no-sharing control that measures attack success from the local model alone; five seeds; bootstrap bands.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Expect the embedding protocol to leak less than parameter sharing, near chance at 1 percent false positives. It may fail for small clients that overfit, where the embeddings themselves memorize members.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Membership and attribute inference over a broad panel of attacks and shared quantities
PROPOSAL: We measure the privacy of exchanging embeddings of a public set against exchanging parameters, logits and gradients. Sixteen clients (ResNet-18, ViT-S, DeiT-S, MobileNetV3, DeiT-Tiny, Swin-T, ConvNeXt-T) train on private CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and CelebA subsets of 20000 images. Attackers with sixteen shadow models run loss-threshold, likelihood-ratio, label-only and attribute inference on each shared quantity, and we report curves for all of them.
CONTROLS: Parameter-sharing averaging for a common architecture; logit sharing; a no-sharing control measuring attack success from the local model; three seeds; bootstrap intervals per attack and each client.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Expect the embedding protocol to leak less than parameter sharing, near chance at 1 percent false positives. It may fail for clients that overfit, where embeddings themselves memorize members.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reliability of centered kernel alignment versus a joint contrastive objective
PROPOSAL: Take four clients with different architectures (ResNet-18, ViT-S, MobileNetV3, DeiT-Tiny) on CIFAR-10 and Flowers-102 tasks. Compare a centered-kernel-alignment proximal term with our joint contrastive objective on a 10000-image public set, and test whether kernel similarity between representation matrices predicts transfer benefit, by correlating it with the change in each client's accuracy on its held-out local test split.
CONTROLS: Local-only training; the proximal term with linear and RBF kernels; permuted-public-set control for the similarity measure; three seeds; rank correlation with bootstrap bands.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Expect kernel similarity to correlate weakly with benefit, below 0.3, while the contrastive objective gains reliably. It may fail if both are equally weak on these small tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Kernel similarity versus joint contrastive objective over a broad grid of settings
PROPOSAL: Take twenty clients with different architectures (ResNet-18, ResNet-50, ViT-S, ViT-B, MobileNetV3, DeiT-S, Swin-T) on CIFAR-100, Flowers-102, DTD and Food-101 tasks. Compare a centered-kernel-alignment proximal term with our joint contrastive objective on a 60000-image public set, and test whether similarity between representation matrices predicts transfer benefit, by correlating it with the accuracy change of each client at six layers and four kernels.
CONTROLS: Local-only training; the proximal term with linear, RBF, polynomial and cosine kernels; permuted-public-set control; three seeds; rank correlation with bootstrap intervals.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Expect kernel similarity to correlate weakly with benefit, below 0.3, while the contrastive objective gains reliably. It may fail if both are equally weak across tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dense prediction clients with non-IID data under joint representation alignment
PROPOSAL: 10 clients with different backbones (ResNet-50, ConvNeXt-T, Swin-T, SegFormer-B0, DeepLabV3-MobileNet, ViT-S) hold non-IID shards for semantic segmentation, depth estimation and surface normals on Cityscapes, NYU and ADE20K. A public set of 40000 unlabeled street and indoor images supports joint alignment of pooled and patch embeddings. We evaluate mean IoU, depth error and angular error per client against local training.
CONTROLS: Local-only training; pairwise InfoNCE on pooled embeddings; patch-level alignment disabled; a Dirichlet partition control with concentration 0.1 and 1.0; five seeds; per-client paired bootstrap.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Expect gains of about two mIoU points for clients with scarce labels. It may fail for surface normals, where pooled embeddings may carry little geometry.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dense prediction at high resolution under joint alignment with long schedules
PROPOSAL: Thirty clients with different backbones (ResNet-101, ConvNeXt-B, Swin-T, SegFormer-B5, DeepLabV3-MobileNet, ViT-B) hold non-IID shards for semantic segmentation, depth estimation, surface normals and panoptic labeling on Cityscapes, NYU, ADE20K and COCO-Stuff at full resolution. A public set of 400000 unlabeled images supports joint alignment of pooled and patch embeddings at four pyramid levels over two hundred rounds. We evaluate mean IoU, depth error and angular error per client.
CONTROLS: Local-only training; pairwise InfoNCE on pooled embeddings; patch-level alignment disabled; Dirichlet partitions with concentration from 0.1 to 1.0; five seeds; per-client paired bootstrap.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Expect gains of about two mIoU points for clients with scarce labels. It may fail for surface normals, where embeddings may carry little geometry.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Minimal test of joint versus pairwise alignment on a synthetic three-client problem
PROPOSAL: Generate three clients from a shared latent code z of dimension 8: each observes a different nonlinear view (a 2-layer MLP, a small CNN on 28x28 rendered digits, a transformer on tokenized code). We train encoders with a joint volume-based contrastive loss and with pairwise InfoNCE, then fit linear probes for a latent factor and for a task label specific to each client, and test the claimed link between the loss and a lower bound on total correlation.
CONTROLS: Pairwise InfoNCE; a loss with permuted positives; an encoder trained on one view only; analytic total correlation of the generator as ground truth; three seeds; bootstrap bands.
COST: 40
PREDICTION: Expect the joint loss to recover latent factors that pairwise sums miss, with probe error lower by about 10 percent. It may fail if the generator's dependence is purely pairwise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Synthetic dependency benchmark with many views and thousands of generator settings
PROPOSAL: Generate twenty clients from shared latent codes of dimension 8, 16 and 32: each observes a different nonlinear view (MLPs, small CNNs on rendered digits, transformers on tokenized code) over 5000 generator settings that vary the order of dependence. We train encoders with a joint volume-based contrastive loss and with pairwise InfoNCE, then fit linear probes for latent factors and for a client-specific task, and test the claimed link to a lower bound on total correlation.
CONTROLS: Pairwise InfoNCE; a loss with permuted positives; an encoder trained on one view only; analytic total correlation of the generator as ground truth; five seeds; bootstrap intervals over all settings.
COST: 40
PREDICTION: Expect the joint loss to recover latent factors that pairwise sums miss, with probe error lower by about 10 percent. It may fail if the generator dependence is purely pairwise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: End-to-end federated multi-task study with foundation-model clients and a joint objective
PROPOSAL: Twenty clients choose foundation models by resource tier (CLIP ViT-B/16, DINOv2-S, DeiT-S, ConvNeXt-T, Swin-T, MobileViT) and fine-tune with adapters on private data for classification, segmentation, depth and captioning on CIFAR-100, ADE20K, NYU and COCO. A public set of 100000 unlabeled images supports joint alignment. We evaluate the final accuracy, the communication per round, and whether gains hold as clients join late.
CONTROLS: Local-only training; pairwise InfoNCE; kernel alignment proximal term; logit distillation among same-task clients; five seeds; paired bootstrap per client; a late-joiner ablation.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: Expect average gains of two points with late joiners recovering most of them within 20 rounds. It may fail if the tasks with dense outputs are not served by pooled embeddings.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Production-scale federation: sixty heterogeneous clients, five task families, one joint objective
PROPOSAL: Each of sixty clients picks a foundation model by resource tier (CLIP ViT-B/32, DINOv2-B, DeiT-B, ConvNeXt-T, Swin-T, EVA-02, SigLIP, MobileViT) and fully fine-tunes it on private data for classification, segmentation, depth, captioning or retrieval, using CIFAR-100, ADE20K, NYU, COCO or LAION subsets. The server receives embeddings of 1000000 public unlabeled images and aligns them jointly across 400 rounds. Outcomes are accuracy, bytes per round, and recovery of late-joining clients.
CONTROLS: Local-only training; pairwise InfoNCE; kernel alignment proximal term; logit distillation among same-task clients; three seeds; paired bootstrap per client; a late-joiner ablation at five join times.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: Expect average gains of two points with late joiners recovering most within 20 rounds. It may fail if the dense-output tasks are not served by pooled embeddings.
